lens: evidence integrity, privacy, and safe action; scoped to state_and_effect_clarity and evidence_trust

findings.criterion: identity binding must remain visibly unbound until source-level review
findings.observation: The ambiguous-identity screen says that no person is selected, but it is already framed by the Alex Chen / Aurora relationship header and permits attaching the source to the current relationship without showing the source fragment or phone clue being bound. The UI therefore biases the decision toward a preselected relationship while withholding the evidence needed to judge the binding.
findings.user_impact: A recruiter can persist private evidence under the wrong person or Pursuit after a superficially explicit but under-informed review, contaminating later facts, actions, and relationship history.
findings.recommendation: Render an unbound identity-review header, show the exact governed source fragment and identity clue beside both temporal candidates, and require an explicit source-to-person-and-Pursuit confirmation. Preserve an undoable, audited binding; keep attach disabled for unresolved or historical-only evidence.
findings.verification: Seed a same-name current/historical-owner case. Assert that the initial screen contains no selected person or Pursuit, that the exact source and clue provenance are inspectable, that unresolved/historical choices cannot bind, and that only an explicit current-interval confirmation creates a reversible binding.

findings.criterion: a confirmed fact revision must remain identical and attributable through downstream effect review
findings.observation: The fact editor accepts any non-empty replacement and labels it a supported value, but the confirmed dependency, approval context, receipt, and history remain hard-coded to Sep 2. The edit is neither marked as recruiter-authored nor carried as the authority-owning revision, so the displayed confirmation can diverge from the state and effect that follow.
findings.user_impact: A recruiter can believe a corrected deadline was confirmed while the product proceeds with stale state and records a different value, weakening both provenance and the validity of the later action approval.
findings.recommendation: Create a typed fact revision that records value, evidence basis, editor, timestamp, and status. Carry its immutable revision or fingerprint through the dependency view, exact-effect approval, receipt, and history; invalidate any action approval whenever that revision changes.
findings.verification: Edit the deadline to Sep 5, confirm it, and assert that every downstream view and audit record shows Sep 5 with recruiter-authored provenance. Edit again after approval and assert that execution is blocked until the changed effect is re-approved.

findings.criterion: exact-effect approval and verified outcome must expose matching destination fields
findings.observation: The approval preview names a Pursuit context and time but omits the reminder destination/list, title or body, and timezone. Reconciliation then advances from a generic exact-ID claim to a verified receipt that shows only time, owner, and operation ID; the recruiter never sees an approved-payload versus observed-payload comparison or mismatch path.
findings.user_impact: The user may approve or later trust a reminder whose actual destination or content differs from intent, while the VERIFIED label overstates what the visible receipt proves.
findings.recommendation: Preview every destination field that will be written and bind it to an effect fingerprint. On reconciliation, display the destination readback, match or mismatch status, observation time, and safe recovery options; permit VERIFIED only after the exact approved payload is observed.
findings.verification: Exercise changed title, list, timezone, permission revocation, timeout, duplicate operation ID, and mismatched readback. Assert that no case reaches VERIFIED unless the destination returns the same effect fingerprint and fields shown at approval.

strengths: The Fact → Effect → Outcome rail, separate fact confirmation, and separately worded exact-effect approval make the intended authority gates unusually legible.
Unknown and failed outcomes avoid optimistic success language, retain the original operation ID, discourage blind retry, and preserve the confirmed fact independently of the action result.
Insufficient evidence and no-action are first-class outcomes; the clarifying message remains visibly DRAFT · NOT SENT, and the historical identity clue cannot be directly attached.
missing_evidence: No freeze-candidate.json exists in the evaluation bundle, so the post screenshots are not cryptographically bound to the reviewed source; Prototype.tsx was modified after the post captures.
No current executable integration evidence proves permission-at-use, durable operation-ID storage, idempotency, destination readback, mismatch reconciliation, reversal, or deletion behavior.
No application-level test exercises edited-fact propagation, ambiguous source-to-person binding, or approved-payload versus readback equivalence.
vetoes: Active veto: wrong or unresolved identity can be persisted because the ambiguous binding flow is pre-framed by a person/Pursuit and allows attachment without displaying the source evidence being bound.
open_questions: What exact source fragment and phone-clue record are being attached in the ambiguous flow, and which server-side authority check rejects a stale or mismatched interval?
Is the local reminder destination an operating-system reminder list, a Talent Signal internal object, or another store, and which exact fields form its idempotent effect fingerprint?
When a recruiter edits a source-derived value, is that value intended to remain source-supported, become a recruiter-authored assertion, or require new evidence?
